entry.content:
Toyota's Land Cruiser started in 1951 as the Jeep BJ and became the Land Cruiser in 1954, once Toyota had to drop the Jeep name, which belonged to Willys-Overland. The 75th Anniversary Special Edition, built on the Land Cruiser 250, is sold through Toyota Germany and limited to 75 vehicles. It is fitted with round headlights with a retro look, 18-inch wheels, and badges at the back and in the cabin, and Smoky Blue, a paint reserved for this edition, is optional. Each buyer also receives a gift box with an enamel sign, a 1:60-scale Tomica model car, a handmade leather key fob, and an updated edition of Alexander Wohlfarth's book Legend Land Cruiser.

entry.summary: Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial car
entry.content:
Lüm-Tec has built watches for the U.S. government and SWAT teams, and its own Combat B line was tested in desert heat and on frozen mountaintops. The Combat B72's 43mm stainless steel case is forged for strength, bead-blasted against scratches and coated in gunmetal. Its dial carries more than 30 layers of Super-Luminova, a glow-in-the-dark material, over a reflective base. A domed sapphire crystal cuts glare, and the watch is water resistant to 656 feet, with double seals at the crown and threaded caseback. Its strap lugs curve downward to wrap the wrist, so it wears smaller than it measures. Two nylon straps, in black and gray, are looped through both sides, so the watch stays on the wrist even if a spring bar, the pin holding a strap end, is damaged. Lüm-Tec replaces the battery and pressure-tests it free for life, and only 500 numbered pieces will be made worldwide.

entry.content:
CountyComm, founded in Sunnyvale, California, in 1992, designs and manufactures gear for government agencies, and its Maratac brand translates that expertise to equipping civilian adventures. Originally used to snag trip wires, the Maratac Grappling Hooks are made in three sizes: the half-ounce Pico and 1.5-ounce Micro in stainless steel, and the 5-ounce Pocket with an aluminum body. Every size has an O-ring-sealed compartment for storage, and the Pocket's stainless steel spikes unscrew and stow inside its body.

entry.content:
At just two pounds, the DMOS Nomad Pro delivers more than twice the strength of the original Nomad without adding weight. The upgraded design integrates the aluminum shaft directly into the shovel head and increases the weld area by 60%, creating a stronger connection for digging through soil, sand, and snow. An improved blade angle makes the compact shovel more comfortable to use, while its 8-gauge 6061 aluminum construction keeps weight to a minimum. Extending to 33 inches and packing down to just 17.5 inches, it's a capable tool for camping, overlanding, and days at the beach, complete with a built-in bottle opener.

entry.content:
Detroit startup Livaq's EQUAD is a 4x4 with an electric motor built into each wheel. It reaches 60 mph in under 7 seconds and tops out at 75 mph, and its swappable battery carries it more than 170 miles and charges wirelessly at home. The body panels are carbon fiber instead of plastic, and the EQUAD is quiet enough, at under 40 decibels, to let you still hear nature around you as you drive the trail. Ground clearance is 12.5 inches, and with water-resistant electronics you may brave a shallow river crossing. Preorders are open.

entry.content:
Held annually between 1980 and 2000, the Camel Trophy was a grueling off-road competition held on some of the Earth's most challenging terrain. Land Rovers were used for the majority of those years, including the Range Rover TD for the 1987 Madagascar race. One of those can be seen in this color photo from Martyn Goddard, who captured it being winched out of the Herefordshire mud during training in January 1986. The photo is printed on Fuji crystal archive paper, numbered and certified, and comes encased inside a hand-made solid wood white or black frame that's ready to hang. Limited edition of 495.

entry.content:
A. Lange & Söhne's Datograph Perpetual, the brand's first wristwatch to combine a chronograph, perpetual calendar and outsize date when it debuted in 2006, returns with a 950 platinum case and five-row bracelet. The black dial carries eleven baguette-cut diamond hour markers, with the 4 and 8 o'clock markers left out to make room for rhodium-colored subdials. The hand-wound L952.1 caliber has 556 parts, 223 of them in the calendar, and a column-wheel flyback chronograph that measures to one-fifth of a second, visible through the sapphire caseback. Production is limited to 50 pieces.
